snippet.title: Jennie’s MMA Performance Had Me Conflicted
snippet.description:
In this video, I give my honest thoughts on Jennie’s MMA performance. This is NOT hate and this is NOT anti behavior. I genuinely enjoyed the performance overall. The remix was top tier, the choreography was clean, the dancers did amazing, and the stage production was solid. From the lighting to the transitions, the creative team did their job.

However, the more I rewatched Jennie’s MMA stage, the more I started noticing certain things, especially when it comes to stamina, energy, and vocals. While there were live moments, a large portion of the performance relied heavily on backing track, and it became more obvious in the second half of the stage. There were moments where Jennie would start a line and then stop singing halfway through, letting the track take over.

What stood out to me the most is that Jennie seemed visibly tired on stage, even early on. This is especially noticeable when comparing the live MMA performance to her rehearsal or dance practice video, where she actually gave more energy. While it makes sense that singing and dancing at the same time is harder, it still raises questions when the live stage relies so much on lip syncing.

This video also talks about performance standards, stamina, and why comparison in K-pop is unavoidable. I bring up other iconic MMA performances, discuss what makes a performance truly legendary, and explain why enjoying a stage doesn’t mean it’s immune to critique. I also talk about why overpraising the bare minimum doesn’t help artists grow in the long run.

Again, this video is not meant to drag Jennie. I like Jennie. I enjoyed the stage. This is simply an honest breakdown from a K-pop fan who watches a lot of performances across different industries. As K-pop becomes more global, it also becomes more open to global criticism, comparison, and discussion.

If you enjoy honest K-pop commentary, long-form performance breakdowns, and respectful discussion, make sure to subscribe, like the video, and comment your thoughts. If you’re watching on mobile and have the Hype feature, please hype the video — it helps the algorithm a lot.

If you watched until the end, comment “honest takes only” so I know you made it all the way through.
